# Navigation overlay UI visibility (2026-02-03 19:45Z)

_**User**_

during navigation the user can reverse the route and navigation instructions are shown using the navigationoverlaykit. 

Extend the functionality:

When the user taps the navigationoverlay the navigation buttons at the top as well as the tab-bar at the bottom should be dismissed/fade out. 

When the user taps the screen then again all those buttons that were hidden should appear again (fade/animate in).

Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\\\\\\\\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\\\\\\\\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\\\\\\\\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\\\\\\\\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"name: Navigation Overlay Mode\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"overview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"todos:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  - Navigation Overlay Mode\\\\\\\\noverview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\\\\\\\\ntodos:\\\\\\\\n  - id: overlay-wireup\\\\\\\\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into docs-changelog\\\\\\\\n    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs\\\\\\\\n    status: completed\\\\\\\\nisProject: false\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Implementation plan\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\\\\\\\\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\\\\\\\\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\\\\\\\\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\\\\\\\\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\\\\\\\\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\\\\\\\\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\\\\\\\\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\\\\\\\\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\\\\\\\\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"name: Navigation Overlay Mode\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"overview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"todos:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  - Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\\\\\\\\n- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&#96; draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. Auto‑centering gating is unified across views.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; uses &#96;MKRoute&#96;, &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96;, and &#96;SettingsManager.navigationTransportType&#96; to render routes and progress; it recalculates on transport changes or movement thresholds and enforces a daily route‑request limit.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;NavigationOverlayKit&#96; is used in &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; to show live turn‑by‑turn instructions when routing from the current device toward the target device.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96; estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; progress overlay rendering splits polylines into completed/remaining segments.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; is backed by &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96; for cached updates; &#96;MapCompass&#96; is shared.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96; groups arrow indicators by edge and scales coordinates; segments represent ~50 km and are capped at 10.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and label components use rasterized caching keyed by color/icon/height/colorScheme/scale and respect Dynamic Type and color scheme.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":67},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; This fresh approach appears to enhance the top bar navigation visually!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1695,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"                  \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"I'm looking into how the TabView applies some properties, specifically using &amp;#96;.toolbarBackground(.hidden, for: .tabBar)&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;.toolbarBackgroundVisibility(.hidden)&amp;#96;. **Commit:** `adf47c5a` — *Navigation: hide/show chrome on overlay or map tap, move accessory/scale bar down when hidden*

**Files changed (3):**

1. **`iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift`**
   - **Chrome visibility:** `isChromeVisible` state drives top toolbar and tab bar visibility; tapping the navigation overlay **toggles** (hide/show), tapping the map **shows** chrome.
   - **Toolbar/tab bar:** `.toolbar(.visible/.hidden)` for navigation bar and tab bar; `.toolbarBackgroundVisibility` for tab bar so it animates off-screen.
   - **Map tap:** `TapGesture` on
